title: Tell the tree what the eye sees
prompt:
Ticketly's Friday price (`#fri-price`) is struck through and greyed out because the date is sold out, but a screen reader only hears "SAR 180". Meanwhile every decorative SVG icon can be announced as an unlabeled graphic.

1. Add the words **sold out** to `#fri-price` so they reach the accessibility tree. You can show them, or hide them visually with a `.visually-hidden` class (not `display: none`).
2. Hide all four decorative `<svg>` icons from assistive technology.
3. Leave Saturday (`#sat-price`) available.
hints: Text that is display: none or visibility: hidden is removed from the accessibility tree too, so it won't be announced.
A visually-hidden class clips the element to 1px with position: absolute, overflow: hidden and clip-path: inset(50%).
Decorative icons get aria-hidden="true" on the <svg> element itself.
explanation: The strike-through is purely visual, so the meaning needs text. A `(sold out)` keeps the words in the accessibility tree while the design stays as it was; plain visible text would be just as valid, and arguably better for sighted users who miss the strike-through. The icons add nothing the text doesn't already say, so `aria-hidden="true"` removes them from the tree and keeps the announcement short: "Friday, heading level 3. 12 June, 8 pm. SAR 180 (sold out)".

checks.sold-out-text: The Friday price contains the words "sold out"
checks.sold-out-in-tree: The "sold out" text is not hidden from assistive technology
checks.icons-hidden: All four decorative icons are hidden with aria-hidden="true"
checks.saturday-available: Saturday still shows SAR 180 and is not marked sold out
